text: In this age of AI, writing every letter by hand has become incredibly more valuable, and I can prove it . I’ve been watching the TV series Pluribus, where one alien consciousness governs all of society. It has somehow absorbed all human consciousness, so it knows every book, every paper, it knows everything. As it moves forward, we find out that the main character is a writer, she begins to write a new book, and the alien being shows a desire to read something new. Thanks for reading! Subscribe for free to receive new posts and support my work. Writing has become a more valuable skill on that matter, we underestimate the human creativity and the inability of AI to create new stuff. I’m pretty bullish on it tough, handmade articles, books, and software can really be a stand out. Recently in the world of databases, Jepsen has published a report on a vibe-coded DBMS called ParticleDB, it’s brutal, they were completely crushed. Here’s the report . I've never seen such a poorly implemented database as this one. I’ve been watching the egress db , a Zig implementation of Postgres, then I found out it was entirely written by AI, unfortunately. It will eventually fall into the same category of slop. This report shows how AI is not ready, they can’t write perfect software, neither can I, that’s for sure. Neither can you, but I’m still bullish on perfecting it . On this talk , Andrew Kelley says “software should be perfect” , it has never left my mind since then. Software can be perfect, or at least very close; we don't see many of these anymore, but they do exist. Right now I have around 4 readers, which is awesome! 4 people worldwide who want to read what I’ve written. But when I compare myself to other newsletters and creators, I’m falling way behind, but it doesn't matter, audience is not the point, it has never been . It reminded me a blog post I read long time ago, “Your likes, hearts, and flattering comments are bad for my brain” from DHH , the numbers can blur our vision, lead us to the easy path. It pushes me to learn more English, programming, poetry, stuff I enjoy. Don't let them exploit your biological bias. For better or worse, our brain works on a specific way which tends to rewards certain behaviours, which is why doomscrolling is so tempting, or why eating the most sugar after the first bite feels so rewarding. The same applies to the numbers; they distort our views perspective the circumstances we're in. It doesn't matter the noise; I'm still bullish on studying, perfecting my craft, regardless what the AI tech lords say. Thanks for reading!
